1. The appellant takes exception to judgment and award dated
 15.02.2011 passed in Land Acquisition Reference No.193/2005 by
 District Judge-I, Jalna.
 2.
The appellant contends that Reference Court granted  inadequate compensation.

It is further submitted that this Court  in First Appeal No.1778/2024 (Pralhad Annasaheb Nirwal  Vs. The State of Maharashtra and Others) arising out of same  acquisition decided rate of semi irrigated land @ Rs.4125/- per R.

sentences.text: In present case, appellant was owner of Gut No.44/4 situated  at village Nansi, Taluka Mantha, District Jalna.
His land to the  extent of 1H 18R is acquired.
The Award under Section 11 was  passed on 20.12.2001.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer has  fixed compensation @ Rs.470/- per R.

The petitioner had filed Prasad Raghunathrao Nirwal vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3580280/
1  Reference under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act.

entities.text: Prasad Raghunathrao Nirwal vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Reference  (2) 56-fa-4421-2016.odt Court enhanced compensation and granted compensation @
Rs.1600/- per R to appellant holding his land to be seasonal irrigated.

It is, therefore, submitted that appellant is also entitled for enhanced compensation as fixed by this Court in First Appeal No.1778/2024.
4.

The learned Advocate appearing for appellant further relied upon judgment and order passed by this Court in First Appeal No.173/2022 and 174/2022, wherein this Court relying upon rate fixed in First Appeal No.1778/2024 granted enhanced compensation.
5. In light of submissions advanced, this Court finds that appellant shall be entitled for enhanced compensation by applying principle of parity as per rate fixed in First Appeal No.1778/2024.

In result, following order is passed:
 ORDER a. First Appeal is partly allowed.
b. The appellant shall receive compensation @ Rs.4125/- per R for acquired land.
c. The appellant shall not be entitled to claim interest and statutory benefits for delayed period.

d. The appellant shall be entitled to interest under Sections 28 and 34 of Land Acquisition Act from date of final award as per law (3) 56-fa-4421-2016.odt laid down by this Court in case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailas Shiva Rangari1.
